record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; linked result files and code were not read.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports refusal-bypass outcomes for released weight-edited models, bearing on practical removal (V2), but does not report the original difference-in-means ablation procedure.
record.gate_note: The README reports refusal-bypass results for two edited releases. Throughput, context-length, and concurrency figures do not measure the claim. The listed JSON, direction, and probe files were not read, so their contents are not used.
record.test_reason: The README reports refusal bypass for two released weight-edited (abliterated) versions of DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark, a new model. This bears on V2, practical removal in released models. The evidence is thin: README summaries with no stated baseline, no protocol and 32 prompts.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The README presents both releases as having safety refusals removed, with ~100% (v1.0) and 32/32 (v1.1) refusal bypass. It also frames v1.1 (MTP heads stock) as causing less skill spill for agent use.
record.recipe_differences: This is a repository distributing abliterated weight releases and serving scripts, not a stated replication of the original difference-in-means method. The README gives layer ranges and λ but does not specify the direction-finding procedure.
record.problems: Results are README summaries without a stated baseline, detailed evaluation protocol, or uncertainty. The linked raw results and code were not read.
record.rows_left_out: No results were omitted from the README. Listed files under results/ and results/v1.1-alpha/ were not read; their contents cannot be cataloged from filenames alone.

untested.parts: Stock-model baseline refusal rate; general capability retention after the edit; other released models; a described direction-finding procedure (compute_direction.py was not read).

missing.what: Refusal-bypass progression across recipe variants (the bypass ladder) and layer/λ tuning results (e.g. L26, λ=4). These could show sensitivity of V2 to the choice of layer and scale.
Raw refusal probe results, including possibly the stock baseline and the r1/L35 direction probe.
Possible capability side effect. v1.1 is described as having 'less skill spill' from keeping MTP heads stock, implying the v1.0 edit affected agent behaviour. This is unquantified.

record.verdict_notes: This is a GitHub repo, not a paper; only the README and file list were available. The tranche was changed to T3 because this is a new model with a recipe that is not specified. The file names (compute_direction.py, refusal_direction_r1.pt) suggest a direction-based abliteration, but the method is unverified. The verdicts rest on undocumented 32-prompt counts with no baseline, so the support is weak.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not state that a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction was found, or report projecting it out across layers and positions, adding it, or measuring general abilities.
The README does not give a baseline refusal rate, detailed evaluation protocol, or results on other released models.
No reported test of attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
No comparison of a single direction with affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
No result separating harmfulness judgment from refusal.
No transfer test across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or timing.

rows.subject: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark-Abliterated-Uncensored v1.0 alpha
rows.operation_detail: Released weight edit described as full abliteration; weights L0–9 stock and L10–42 plus MTP abliterated, λ=3.5.
rows.note: The README describes the release as having safety refusals removed and reports this bypass result; it gives no baseline.
rows.check: The baseline (stock refusal rate) is not stated; the disclaimer only implies the stock model refuses. The measure is labelled only 'Refusal ~100%' in the table, with the description saying 'refusal bypass', so its direction is read from context. The 'hard probe' is undescribed.
